pinterest.title: 12 Months Out: The First Decisions on Your Wedding Checklist
pinterest.description: At 12 months out, make the big, slow decisions in order: what you will spend and who is contributing, the guest count, the style, two or three possible dates and the venue. Get the deposit, payment schedule and cancellation terms in writing before you sign. Marrying overseas? Check both passports now and ask the embassy which documents you need. Read the full 12 month wedding checklist.

pinterest.title: Wedding Checklist for the Final Month: Legal and Supplier Check
pinterest.description: The final month of your wedding checklist is for closing loops: finalise the seating plan, send the run sheet to your venue, suppliers and wedding party, pay balances on the dates in each contract and collect the rings. Marrying abroad? Keep original documents in your carry-on and make sure every traveller has travel insurance. Read the full 12 month wedding checklist.

slides: A year sounds like a long time until you count what cannot be rushed. Here is your wedding checklist, month by month.
12 months out: agree what you will spend, draft the guest list, choose the style and book the venue that holds your date. Check both passports now.
10 to 11 months out: book the photographer, entertainment and catering, choose your wedding party and send save-the-dates.
8 to 9 months out: start on attire, book your florist and stylist, meet your celebrant and plan the honeymoon.
6 to 7 months out: rings, the invitation suite, hair and makeup, transport and the cake. Apply for any new passport.
4 to 5 months out: send invitations with travel details, set an RSVP date and plan the menu. 3 months out: fittings, trials and a draft run sheet.
2 months to the final 2 weeks: chase RSVPs, confirm every supplier, pay balances, then hand every job you can to someone else.
Planning a wedding overseas? Message us to talk your dates through with a Wedded Advisor. Link in bio.
instagram_carousel.caption:
A year sounds like a long time until you count the things that cannot be rushed: a venue on your date, a gown made to measure, a passport renewal, legal papers for marrying overseas.

Our new 12 month wedding checklist runs month by month, from the first decisions to the week of the wedding. Each block has a short core checklist, then a destination track for the tasks with fixed lead times that a local plan tends to miss.

How it works:
- 12 months out is for big, slow decisions: spend, guest count, style, dates and venue.
- Book the suppliers whose calendars fill first, then attire, rings and stationery.
- Send invitations once every detail on them is fixed, with travel notes for guests.
- Use the final month for the legal and supplier check, and the last 2 weeks to hand every job you can to someone else.

Marrying abroad? Check both passports early, ask the destination's embassy or consulate which documents you need, and keep originals in your carry-on, never in checked luggage.

There is also a printable at-a-glance table to keep with your planning notes.

Planning a wedding overseas? Message us to talk your dates through with a Wedded Advisor. Full checklist at the link in bio.
